newsitem.title: USA: Hechinger rises on hopes deal gets done.
newsitem.headline: Hechinger rises on hopes deal gets done.

text.p: Shares of Hechinger Co rose about six percent Wednesday on hopes the retailer would complete a sale of the company.
Hechinger's shares rose 12.5 cents to $2.375 in afternoon trading, edging closer to the $3.00 a share pricetag that Hechinger said on Tuesday it could fetch in a sale.

Some Wall Street analysts said Hechinger could be talking to other building supply retailers or hardware chains, including Waban Inc, Sears, Roebuck and Co or Lowe's Cos Inc. But others said a financial bidder is more likely to acquire the company.

Largo, Md.-based Hechinger said Tuesday it was talking with an unnamed suitor about a deal that could result in shareholders receiving $3.00 for each Hechinger share. The retailer said it could not be sure the deal would go through, or if it would be completed at that price.

On Wednesday, Hechinger Chief Financial Officer W. Clark McClelland declined to say whether the bidder was a financial firm or a rival retailer. He also would not estimate when a deal would be unveiled, although he added, "I don't think it will be months."

If Hechinger were to team up with a retailer, it would be the latest combination in a consolidating industry. Last year, Sears bought San Jose, Calif.,-based Orchard Supply Hardware Stores Corp for $415 million and others were expected to disappear due to competition from Home Depot and other giants.
Sears has pushed hard to expand its stand-alone Sears Hardware store chain. Last year, it opened 71 new outlets and planned to have a total of 400 by 2000.
Sears declined to comment on rumors it was looking at Hechinger. Last year, Hechinger flat-out denied it was in talks with Sears about an acquisition.

Hoffman Estates, Ill.,-based Sears was expected to use further acquisitions to expand, analysts said. But Hechinger's sites do not fit with Sears' strategy of avoiding competition with big-box retailers such as Home Depot and staying in smaller, neighborhood markets.

"Sears has a strategy of expanding off-the-mall," said Todd Slater of Lazard Freres & Co. "While Hechinger would satisfy that, its home-building orientation doesn't fit the exact profile (that Sears is looking for)."
Natick, Mass.,-based Waban, parent of HomeBase building supply retail chain, also declined to comment on speculation it could bid for Hechinger.

In April, Waban and Kmart Corp called off talks to merge HomeBase with Kmart's Builders Square division. Under the deal, Leonard Green & Partners LP, an investment banking firm, was to be the chief stockholder in the new company.

Kmart declined to say whether it was considering a combination with Hechinger. The company has continued working with Leonard Green to sell Builders Square, although it would disclose any possible suitors, said spokesman Robert Burton.

A financial player was likely to step to the plate for Hechinger because its fleet of small stores would not be the right size for Home Depot or Lowe's, which both are opening stores bigger than 100,000 square feet, said Kirk Taniguchi ofMerrill Lynch & Co.
Lowe's also declined to comment on speculation about it and Hechinger.
"(The retailers) that have the financial strength to make the acquisition aren't interested," he said. "Another company isn't going to buy out Hechinger just to close up all of its stores."
